body_ar:
حكم التعامل مع مانع الزكاة هل يجوز لشخص مسلم أن يأخذ صدقة من عند مسلم ولكنه يعرف أنه لا يؤدي صدقة ماله أي زكاة ماله فهل يجوز له أن يكون عاملا في ماله مع العلم أنه لا يؤدي زكاة ماله؟

نعم، فالمعاملات لا يمنعها منع الزكاة، إذا كان الإنسان مانعا للزكاة فهذا إسلامه ناقص وقد قال الله تعالى: {وويل للمشركين الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة} وهو أيضا محتجب من تلقاء نفسه عن رحمة الله، وقد قال الله تعالى:{ ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء فسأكتبها للذين يتقون ويؤتون الزكاة}، فرحمة الله هي للذين يتقون ويؤتون الزكاة، والويل هو للذين يمتنعون من أداء الزكاة، وويل للمشركين الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة، لكن مع هذا يجب على من يعامله أن ينصح له فيبين له خطر ما هو عليه، يبين له ما قال النبي (ص) في الصحيحين فقد ذكر النبي (ص) خطرا عظيما يتهدد من لا يؤدي الزكاة ...
body_en:
The ruling on dealing with one who withholds zakat. May a Muslim take charity from a Muslim whom he knows does not render the charity due on his wealth, that is, the zakat on his wealth? And is it permissible for him to work in his wealth, knowing that he does not render the zakat on his wealth?

Yes. Transactions are not barred by the withholding of zakat. If a person withholds zakat, then his submission (islām) is deficient. God Most High has said: {and woe to those who associate partners with God, who do not give the zakat} (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:6–7). He also veils himself, by his own doing, from God's mercy. God Most High has said: {and My mercy encompasses all things; I shall prescribe it for those who are God-conscious and give the zakat} (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:156). God's mercy is for those who are God-conscious and give the zakat, and the woe is for those who refuse to render the zakat — "and woe to those who associate partners with God, who do not give the zakat". Even so, whoever deals with him must give him sincere counsel, making plain to him the danger of the state he is in; let him make plain to him what the Prophet, upon whom be peace, said in the two Ṣaḥīḥs — for the Prophet, upon whom be peace, mentioned a grave danger that threatens the one who does not render the zakat ...

flags.arabic: فقد ذكر النبي (ص) خطرا عظيما يتهدد من لا يؤدي الزكاة ...

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The text stops in the middle of the Sheikh's counsel, at the exact point where he is about to cite the hadith. A reader is left with 'yes, you may deal with him' and no sight of the warning that follows. The full material is behind the .docx download in source_download_link. Option 2 is not acceptable on its own.

flags.arabic: فهل يجوز له أن يكون عاملا في ماله
flags.context: the second limb of the question
options: is it permissible for him to work in his wealth [i.e. be employed by him]
is it permissible for him to act as his agent in his wealth
is it permissible for him to be his partner on a profit-sharing basis (muḍārabah) in his wealth
flags.note: ʿĀmil carries all three senses. In a zakat context ʿāmil is also the collector of zakat, which would be a fourth sense, though the syntax ('ʿāmilan fī mālihi', 'working in his wealth') tells against it. The distinction matters, because the ruling on ordinary wage labour and the ruling on a muḍārabah partnership in wealth on which zakat is unpaid are not obviously the same question. Option 0 is the most literal and leaves the ambiguity where the Arabic leaves it.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.

The date shown by the CMS (27 December 2010) is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends; nothing has been supplied to complete the hadith. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'His submission (islām) is deficient' renders 'fa-hādhā islāmuhu nāqiṣ'. This is a statement about the completeness of his islām, not a declaration of unbelief, and must not be strengthened into one.

The Sheikh cites Fuṣṣilat 41:6–7 twice, the second time without the brace brackets used by the source for the first. The second occurrence is rendered as a quotation within his own sentence, as he gives it.
The verse references have been supplied in the English per house style; the source gives the verse text without any reference.
